findings.title: Validate command ignores the active worktree path
findings.description: `validateFrontmatterAction` destructures only `id` from `resolveProjectWorktree` and passes `project.projectPath` into `validateFrontmatterFiles` at `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:89-103`. `packages/cli/src/utils/project.ts#resolveProjectWorktree` returns a `worktreeId` when cwd matches a registered worktree path, and `packages/cli/src/utils/worktree-overlay.ts:16-24` provides `resolveOperationPath` for exactly this filesystem-path selection, but the new command does not use either. In a worktree, the no-paths mode validates/fixes the main checkout; explicit staged paths resolved from the worktree cwd are outside the main `project-documents/user/` root and are silently skipped by `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterFileValidator.ts#resolveExplicitPaths`. For a pre-commit gate this can report a false green with zero relevant files checked, and `--fix` can mutate the wrong tree. Use the resolved worktree operation path and add a test from a worktree cwd.

findings.title: --fix can exit 0 while a document is still invalid
findings.description: `validateFrontmatter` returns immediately after emitting an inferred `docType` fixAction (`packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:221-229`). The CLI fix loop at `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:109-133` applies that fix, sets `remaining` only from unfixable/failed findings, and never revalidates; output and exit code at `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:136-155` are still based on the original findings. A document missing `docType` but otherwise lacking required fields can therefore be "fixed" to a schema that now requires `project`, `status`, `dateCreated`, and `dateUpdated`, yet the command exits 0 and JSON reports `fixed: 1` with no `fixErrors`. The new tests do not cover missing-`docType` fixes. Either revalidate after `docType` fixes or keep the run non-clean.

findings.title: handleError's second parameter breaks process event listeners
findings.description: `handleError` now accepts `exitCode = 1` and calls `process.exit(exitCode)` at `packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:46-71`. It is still registered directly as `process.on('uncaughtException', handleError)` and `process.on('unhandledRejection', handleError)` at `packages/cli/src/index.ts:171-172`. Node invokes those listeners with a second argument (`origin` string for `uncaughtException`, the rejected promise for `unhandledRejection`), so that value is now passed as the exit code instead of the default `1`. Depending on Node version, `process.exit` will reject the non-numeric argument or coerce it incorrectly, making top-level error handling unreliable. Wrap the listeners, e.g. `(err) => handleError(err)`, or make the second parameter an options object that cannot collide with event-listener signatures.

findings.title: Broad catches collapse unrelated failures into exit 2 and stdout error output
findings.description: The fix-loop catch at `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:118-130` catches every error, records a string, and continues without a comment explaining why swallowing is correct or an ERROR-level log; its messages are printed to stdout by `printHumanOutput` at `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:80-83`. This is not one of the allowed exception patterns in `CLAUDE.md` (specific handled exception with rationale, rethrow after logging, or true process-boundary handler). Separately, the command-level catch at `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:177-181` calls `handleError(err, 2)` for any error thrown by `store.getById` or `validateFrontmatterFiles`, so unexpected storage/I/O failures are classified as "invocation error" even though the documented contract in `CHANGELOG.md:25` reserves 2 for project-resolution failures. Narrow the exit-2 handling to known invocation errors and send fix errors to stderr/logging.

findings.title: Fix actions are applied without validating their type
findings.description: The loop at `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:113-125` treats any `finding.fixAction` as a frontmatter field write. The public type is still a loose `fixAction?: { type: string; field: string; value: string }` at `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:28`, so illegal action variants are representable. `ConsistencyChecker.applyFixes` in `packages/core/src/introspection/ConsistencyChecker.ts#applyFixes` branches on `fixAction.type`; this command skips that check entirely. A future non-frontmatter action would silently be written as YAML with `field`/`value`. Use a discriminated union for fix actions and skip/report unsupported action types explicitly.

findings.title: New docType-constraint test is misleading and provides no coverage
findings.description: The test named "a wrong docType literal is still caught by the value-constraint logic" at `packages/core/tests/schema/frontmatterSchema.test.ts:371-397` does not construct a wrong literal for a registered schema: it passes valid `devlog`, valid `gate-evidence`, and an unknown docType, then expects zero findings for all three. Because `validateFrontmatter` selects the schema by `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS[data.docType]` and returns early when absent (`packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:228-229`), a mistyped or unknown `docType` never reaches the value-constraint loop. The comments at `packages/core/tests/schema/frontmatterSchema.test.ts:389-395` describe the opposite behavior from what is asserted. Add a real regression test for the intended behavior, or rename/rewrite this test to document the unknown-docType pass-through explicitly.

findings.title: Validate tests leak spy implementations between tests
findings.description: The suite installs console/stdout spies in `beforeEach` at `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate.test.ts:52-60`, and the "unresolvable project" test installs a `process.exit` spy at `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate.test.ts:83-91`. There is no `afterEach`/`vi.restoreAllMocks()` in the file; `vi.clearAllMocks()` at line 53 only clears call history and does not restore implementations. With Vitest's default `restoreMocks: false`, later tests in this file run with `process.exit` still stubbed and console/stdout still mocked, so behavior depends on test order and a later unexpected `handleError` call can be hidden. Add per-file mock restoration or configure `restoreMocks`.

structured_findings.summary: Validate command ignores the active worktree path
--fix can exit 0 while a document is still invalid
handleError's second parameter breaks process event listeners
Broad catches collapse unrelated failures into exit 2 and stdout error output
Fix actions are applied without validating their type
New docType-constraint test is misleading and provides no coverage
Validate tests leak spy implementations between tests
